subject: Computer Studies
content: a. Two main constituents of a computer (hardware and software) and characteristics of computers (Electronic, Accuracy, Speed, Interactive, Reliability, Consistency, Large Storage). b. Hardware: Central Processing Unit, Peripherals (Input and Output devices), Storage media; input devices (keyboard, mouse, scanner, joystick, light pen, voice, digital camera) and output devices (monitor, printer, speaker, plotters), including inkjet, laser and line printers. c. CPU components: Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU), Registers - MDR, MAR, MBR, AC, PC, CIR; concepts of bus and address; Primary Memory (RAM, ROM) versus Secondary/auxiliary storage (floppy disks, magnetic tape, hard disks, CD, DVD, USB); storage units (bits, bytes, nibbles, words, kilobytes, megabytes, gigabytes, terabytes) and the Input-Process-Output cycle; factors affecting data transfer speed (bus speed and bus width). d. Logic Circuits: AND, NOT, OR, NOR, NAND gates, their symbols and truth tables, and simple comparators using XOR/NOR gates. e. Software: system software (Operating Systems, Utility Software, Middleware, Device Drivers, Translators) versus application software (Word Processing, Spreadsheet, Database, Presentation, Graphics, Accounting, Payroll, and other off-the-shelf packages); Operating System functions and interfaces (Command-Line, Menu, GUI), examples (MS Windows, LINUX, UNIX, mobile OS); Utility Software (editors, anti-virus); Translators (Interpreter, Assembler, Compiler); open source versus proprietary software and methods of acquiring application software.
objectives: Candidates should be able to: i. define computer system in relation to its nature and programmability; ii. list functional parts of computer systems; iii. explain the characteristics of computers; iv. identify the differences between hardware and software; v. define and give examples of hardware and output devices, list CPU and memory components and explain their functions; vi. distinguish between primary and secondary memory, list types and uses of secondary storage, and relate storage unit measurements; vii. define registers, bus and address, and explain the functions of MDR, MAR, MBR, AC, PC and CIR; viii. state the major steps in converting data to information (Input-Process-Output) and enumerate factors affecting data transfer speed; ix. define logic gates (AND, NOT, OR, NOR, NAND), interpret logic equations, list gate symbols, construct truth tables, and construct a simple comparator; x. differentiate between system and application software, list types of system software, define and list functions/types of Operating Systems and Utility Software, define translators and their categories; xi. list examples of application software, differentiate open source and proprietary software, and explain methods of acquiring application software.

content: a. Full meanings of www, HTTP, HTTPS, HTML, XML and a brief history of www. b. Basic terminologies: WWW, website, homepage, protocol; types of protocols (http, https, ftp). c. subject: Computer Studies
topic_title: Ethical issues, Computer Security and Cyber risks
content: a. Computer-related crime: compromising computer systems, hacking, theft. b. Responsibility for computer failure and protection of computer property, records and software. c. Methods to prevent unauthorized use of computer systems (user identification, passwords) and measures to protect privacy of individuals by law and electronically. d. Computer security types: Network security, Internet (cyber) security, Application Security, Data security, Information security, End user security; security tools (firewalls, antivirus software, encryption). e. Application threat categories (input, authorization, session management, parameter tampering) and basic dimensions of Information Security (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability - CIA). f. Network security issues (unauthorized intrusion) and network security methods (antivirus software, behavioural analytics, data loss prevention, email security, firewalls, mobile device security, network segmentation, SEIM, VPN, web security, wireless security, Network Access Control). g. Types of cyber security threats: cybercrime, cyber-attack, cyber terrorism, malware, virus, trojans, spyware, ransomware, adware, botnets, SQL injection, phishing, man-in-the-middle attack, denial of service. h. Cyber security safety tips: regular software updates, use of anti-virus software, strong passwords, avoiding unknown email attachments/links, avoiding unsecured public WIFI.
objectives: Candidates should be able to: i. define computer-related crime and state examples; ii. list methods to prevent unauthorized use of computer systems; iii. list measures to protect privacy of individuals; iv. define computer security and identify different types of computer security; v. identify appropriate security tools for different types of computer security; vi. identify categories of application threats; vii. identify basic dimensions of information security (CIA); viii. mention network security issues and methods; ix. list types of cyber security threats; x. list cyber security safety tips.
